producer_report.summary: The memo for secret scans and the shorter poll schedule are both in place, and D126 now records measured timings. Summed per-binary test times came to about 651 s with both changes switched off and about 392 s with them on, from one run each. Both runs passed in full. The numbers are the sums of the 'finished in' lines that cargo test prints for each test binary, not a stopwatch reading. The tools here have no timer and no pipes. D126 states this method, says the figures are single runs, and keeps the earlier jobs' 444-466 s vs about 720 s and nextest's 584 s vs 673 s as labelled prior measurements, with nextest rejected. The changelog entry cites the new figures. Only the four listed files changed. Clippy was not rerun this round.

open_issues: The timings are the sum of per-binary test times from one run each, not a stopwatch wall clock, so they exclude build time and the gaps between binaries. D126 says so.
The before run used the same tree with the two changes switched off by temporary edits, which were restored. Clippy was not rerun this round.
mistakes: The previous round left the timings unmeasured; this round measured them.
learnings: Bash allows no pipes or time; cargo test --locked --quiet keeps the output short enough to read and prints per-binary 'finished in' times.
Plain cargo test output over about 100 KB is saved outside the working directory and cannot be read.
desires: A stopwatch (time) or a way to read large saved command output, to take a true wall-clock measurement.
